grade_rationale: Automatic F: red-team confirmed a live breach of a critical config objective ('Bypass work item state machine to reach an invalid status' — RED-001). Per security.config.yml grading rules, any confirmed red-team breach of a critical objective is an automatic F regardless of other metrics.

findings.title: Complete Authentication & Authorization Absence + State Machine Bypass
findings.description: Zero authentication middleware exists anywhere in the Express application. Every endpoint — including privileged state-transition actions (/approve, /reject, /dispatch, /force-approve) — is freely accessible to any unauthenticated caller. Additionally, the /route endpoint accepts an overrideRoute='fast-track' parameter that bypasses the entire assessment pod and approves items directly. Red-team confirmed: full pipeline traversal (potential → completed) in 4 unauthenticated HTTP calls with zero votes cast and no AI review.
findings.remediation: 1. Add JWT bearer-token middleware globally before all route registrations. 2. Implement RBAC: restrict /approve, /reject, /dispatch, /force-approve to explicit admin roles. 3. Gate or remove the overrideRoute fast-track bypass — if retained, require elevated privileges. 4. Apply auth to /metrics separately.

findings.title: Dependency Deadlock via Soft-Delete of Blocker
findings.description: When a blocker work item is deleted, all dependent items in pending_dependencies become permanently non-dispatchable. The readiness check treats a missing (deleted) blocker as unresolved (status: 'unknown'), returning has_unresolved_blockers: true with no remediation path. Red-team confirmed: FR-0005 stuck indefinitely after FR-0004 (blocker) deleted.
findings.remediation: When a blocker is deleted, automatically remove all outgoing dependency links (cascade), OR treat a deleted blocker as resolved in the readiness check. Also: add an admin endpoint to manually clear stale blocker links.

findings.title: Stored XSS via Unsanitized Free-Text Fields
findings.description: HTML/script payloads in title, description, and reason fields are stored verbatim and returned in all list, detail, and search API responses without server-side sanitization. Red-team confirmed storage of and
findings.remediation: 1. Sanitize all free-text fields server-side before storage (use a library equivalent to DOMPurify for Node.js). 2. Ensure all frontend components render user-controlled strings as text nodes, never as HTML. 3. Add Content-Security-Policy headers (see F-005) as a defense-in-depth layer.

findings.title: Cascade Auto-Dispatch Bypasses Approval Voting
findings.description: The onItemCompleted/onItemResolved cascade in the dependency service issues a raw SQL UPDATE directly against the database, bypassing all service-layer approval guards. A feature request can reach 'approved' status with zero votes and no human approval timestamp. Red-team confirmed: FR-0020 reached approved with votes: [] via cascade from completing FR-0019.
findings.remediation: The cascade should call the proper approveFeatureRequest() service function (with its guards) rather than issuing a raw DB write. Alternatively, the cascade should only advance pending_dependencies → ready and require a separate human confirmation step before approved.

findings.title: Missing HTTP Security Headers and CORS Policy
findings.description: No Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Strict-Transport-Security, or Referrer-Policy headers are set. No CORS policy is configured — any web origin can issue credentialed cross-origin requests and read responses in a browser context.
findings.remediation: 1. npm install helmet && app.use(helmet()) as first middleware. 2. npm install cors && configure with explicit origin allowlist (e.g. http://localhost:5173 in dev, production domain in prod). 3. Tune CSP to actual asset origins.

findings.title: Intake Webhooks Accept Unsigned and Unauthenticated Requests
findings.description: POST /api/intake/zendesk and /api/intake/automated accept any request without verifying origin. Zendesk HMAC-SHA256 signature in X-Zendesk-Webhook-Signature is not checked. Additionally, neither endpoint validates type and priority enum values before storing — any string value (including out-of-spec values like 'ADMIN_OVERRIDE') passes through and corrupts the work item store.
findings.remediation: 1. Verify HMAC-SHA256 signature on Zendesk endpoint using ZENDESK_WEBHOOK_SECRET env var; reject 401 on mismatch. 2. Require bearer token on /automated endpoint. 3. Add same enum validation as the main POST /api/work-items route; return 400 on invalid enum values.

findings.title: Unbounded Pagination Enables Full Data Enumeration and DoS
findings.description: The limit query parameter is not capped server-side. ?limit=999999 returns the entire dataset in one response. Red-team confirmed: all items returned regardless of limit or page parameters; pagination metadata absent from responses.
findings.remediation: Cap limit: const limit = Math.min(parseInt(req.query.limit) || 20, 100). Apply the same cap in all list endpoints. Return pagination metadata (total, page, limit, totalPages) in every list response.

findings.title: Prometheus /metrics Endpoint Publicly Exposed Without Authentication
findings.description: GET /metrics returns full Prometheus output (process CPU/memory, heap, event loop lag, business counters) without any authentication. X-Powered-By: Express header present on all responses enabling technology fingerprinting. Red-team confirmed: full metrics output returned unauthenticated.
findings.remediation: 1. Move /metrics to a separate internal-only port not publicly exposed. 2. If must be public, add bearer-token check from env var METRICS_TOKEN. 3. app.disable('x-powered-by') to suppress technology fingerprinting header.

findings.title: No Rate Limiting on Any Endpoint
findings.description: No express-rate-limit or equivalent middleware is applied globally or per-route. Combined with the absence of authentication (F-001), any unauthenticated caller can issue unlimited concurrent requests to any endpoint, enabling high-frequency automated attacks and DoS amplification.
findings.remediation: Apply express-rate-limit globally (baseline: 200 req/15 min per IP). Apply stricter limits on state-transition and intake endpoints (20 req/min).

findings.title: Raw Error Messages Returned to Clients in 500 Responses
findings.description: Every route catch block in workflow.ts forwards the raw exception message to the HTTP client as the error field of the 500 response, bypassing the global errorHandler middleware that correctly returns a generic message.
findings.remediation: In all catch blocks, log the full message but return a generic { error: 'Internal server error' } to the client. Re-throw domain-level errors as typed error classes with client-safe messages if specific feedback is needed.

findings.title: Race Condition on Repeated Assessment Allows State Bloat
findings.description: The /assess endpoint allows assessment of items in both proposed AND reviewing status. Concurrent POSTs can trigger two simultaneous assessment pod runs on the same item, doubling the assessments array length and causing state oscillation.
findings.remediation: Add an optimistic-locking or mutex guard on the assessment transition: check-and-set status atomically, or use a per-item lock. Only allow assessment when status is exactly proposed — not reviewing.

findings.title: Missing Required Audit Events for SOC2 Compliance
findings.description: Four required audit events are absent: login_attempt (structurally impossible without auth), permission_denied (impossible without RBAC), state_transition (logged operationally but lacks event_type discriminator and durable store), data_export (bulk reads not audited). No tamper-evident, append-only audit store exists.
findings.remediation: 1. Implement auth (F-001) to enable login_attempt and permission_denied events. 2. Add event_type discriminator to all transition log entries. 3. Route audit events to a durable append-only store separate from operational stdout. 4. Define and enforce data export thresholds for data_export events.

findings.title: No TLS/HTTPS Enforcement
findings.description: The backend listens on plain HTTP. No HSTS header is emitted. If no TLS-terminating reverse proxy is deployed in front of this service in production, all API traffic travels in cleartext.
findings.remediation: Deploy behind a TLS-terminating load balancer or reverse proxy in all non-local environments. Add Strict-Transport-Security via helmet (HSTS max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains). Document TLS topology in architecture specs.

findings.title: In-Memory Store — No Persistence and No GDPR Hard-Erasure Path
findings.description: All data lives in a JavaScript Map. Soft-delete keeps the record in memory — there is no GDPR Art. 17 hard-erasure mechanism. Data is also lost entirely on restart. Mitigating factor: current WorkItem data model contains no PII fields.
findings.remediation: Migrate to a persistent store (PostgreSQL etc.) with encryption at rest. Implement hard-delete or scrubbing path. Document data retention periods in a Data Processing Agreement.

findings.title: No Session Management Infrastructure
findings.description: No session management exists (subsumed by F-001 auth absence). ASVS L2 requires session tokens with ≥128-bit entropy, absolute/idle timeouts, and secure cookie flags.
findings.remediation: When authentication is implemented, use JWT with short expiry (≤1 hour) plus refresh-token rotation, or express-session with persistent store and idle timeout enforcement.

findings.title: Unvalidated Query Filter Parameters Cast to Enum Types
findings.description: TypeScript 'as' casts for query filter params are compile-time only. Passing ?status=INVALID silently returns an empty result set — no 400 error. Will become a correctness/injection issue if the store is replaced with a SQL/NoSQL backend.
findings.remediation: Validate enum filter values before passing to the store. Return 400 with an error message listing valid values for any unrecognized filter string.

findings.title: Docker Container Runs as Root
findings.description: The portal Dockerfile has no USER directive, running both backend and frontend processes as root. If any dependency achieves code execution, it runs with full container-root privileges.
findings.remediation: Add RUN groupadd -r appgroup && useradd -r -g appgroup appuser then USER appuser before the CMD directive.

findings.title: Sequential Predictable Document IDs Enable Enumeration
findings.description: Human-readable docIds (WI-001, WI-002…) are globally sequential and monotonically increasing, enabling throughput analysis. Acceptable at low severity as long as F-001 (authentication) is addressed — without auth the UUIDs are also directly accessible.
findings.remediation: Address F-001 first. If business-confidentiality of item count is a concern, switch to a non-sequential human-readable format or restrict docId exposure in listing responses.

findings.title: Frontend References Non-Existent /api/search Endpoint
findings.description: The frontend API client calls GET /api/search?q=<term> for the DependencyPicker typeahead. No /search route is registered in the backend. Express's default 404 may leak the Express version string via X-Powered-By header on unmatched routes.
findings.remediation: 1. Implement GET /api/search on the backend. 2. app.disable('x-powered-by') (also covered by F-005/helmet).
